Tabular prediction summary for a dataset

bl_predict.Rd

Scores every row of a data frame through the fitted model and returns a tidy data frame suitable for inspection and target selection. This replaces the ad-hoc data.frame() construction used in example scripts.

Usage

bl_predict(bl_result, data = NULL)

Arguments

bl_result

A "bl_result" object from bl_assemble.

data

Data frame to score. Defaults to bl_result$test_data.

Value

A data frame with columns row, pred_prob, pred_class, optionally true_class and confusion, followed by all feature columns.

Details

The returned data frame contains:

  • row — row index (1-based).

  • pred_prob — model predicted probability (rounded to 3 d.p.).

  • pred_class — predicted class (0 or 1).

  • true_class — true class if a "class" column is present in data; otherwise omitted.

  • confusion — "TP", "TN", "FP", or "FN" if true class is known; otherwise omitted.

  • One column per feature variable from bl_result$var_names.

Examples

bl_dat  <- bl_prepare_data(datasets::iris, class_col = "Species",
                            target_class = "versicolor")
#> Hull fraction: 0.90 | Retained: 110 (91.7%) | Removed: 10 (8.3%)
bl_mod  <- bl_fit_model(bl_dat$train_data, bl_dat$var_names)
bl_proj <- bl_build_projection(bl_dat$train_data, bl_dat$var_names)
bl_grid <- bl_build_grid(bl_dat$train_data, bl_proj, bl_mod, m = 50L)
result  <- bl_assemble(bl_dat, bl_model = bl_mod,
                        bl_projection = bl_proj, bl_grid = bl_grid)

# Inspect test-set predictions
bl_predict(result)
